comparator.name: Human Resource Studies (Personeelwetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: 2025–26 detailed public curriculum with 2026–27 OER confirmation, checked 2026-10-06
comparator.sourceNotes: The detailed official programme page available on the check date still labels its curriculum 2025–26, while Tilburg’s official OER portal lists the programme in the current 2026–27 regulations. The published detailed structure accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in each of years 1 and 2, then a 30-ECTS open mobility window, one 6-ECTS constrained professionalisation elective, two further 6-ECTS courses and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded. The discrepancy is preserved rather than silently relabeling the detailed table.

components.note: One of two constrained 6-ECTS professionalisation electives is instantiated neutrally.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The official detailed curriculum requires one of two 6-ECTS professionalisation electives without identifying either as the general route. Coaching en Ontwikkeling is listed first and is therefore instantiated as a neutral official-order tie-break; the choice was made before and independently of UCR course selection.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme owns strategic HRM, people analytics, evidence-based decisions, financial consequences, teamwork and the general people-work-organisation relationship. Workplace psychology, health, well-being and development form a coherent second route, while labour relations, employment law and the future of work form a distinct institutional route. Both exceed the 30-ECTS distinctness floor. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible interest has one construction owner.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dedicated HRM sequence with labour law, work-and-health psychology, people analytics, consulting, a professionalisation elective and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can construct coherent interdisciplinary routes in people and organisations, workplace psychology and labour institutions, but it does not reproduce the complete specialist HRM or methods sequence; the 30-ECTS open mobility space remains unfilled.
The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.

On 6 October 2026 Tilburg’s detailed public curriculum table was still labelled 2025–26, while the official OER portal listed current 2026–27 regulations for B Personeelwetenschappen. The comparison preserves that discrepancy and does not claim the detailed table itself is labelled 2026–27.
